name: Everglades National Park
summary: The 'river of grass' — a vast subtropical wetland and the only place on earth where alligators and crocodiles coexist, best seen by airboat and boardwalk.

lodging.name: Stay in Homestead or Everglades City
lodging.blurb: Homestead for the main entrances; Everglades City for the Gulf side.

foodMustTry.name: Stone crab & gator bites
foodMustTry.blurb: Everglades City stone crab in season, and a fried-gator sampler.

days.label: Day 230 — Shark Valley & an airboat
days.summary: Alligators from the tower and the swamp by airboat.

item.title: Shark Valley tram & tower
item.blurb: Bike or ride the tram on the 15-mile loop past gators to the observation tower over the sawgrass.

item.title: Everglades airboat tour
item.blurb: A classic fan-boat blast through the grass with a naturalist.

item.title: The Skunk Ape HQ & the smallest post office in America
item.blurb: Ochopee, population a few dozen, has both. The Skunk Ape Research Headquarters has been hunting Florida's swamp bigfoot since the 1970s and sells the T-shirt; a mile down the road the United States Post Office operates out of a 7-by-8-foot irrigation shed, the smallest in the country, and it will postmark anything you hand it.

days.label: Day 231 — Anhinga Trail & Flamingo
days.summary: The park's wildlife-rich heart, down to Florida Bay.

item.title: Anhinga Trail & the road to Flamingo
item.blurb: An easy boardwalk crowded with gators, anhingas, and herons, then the drive to Flamingo on Florida Bay.

commute.scenicNote: South onto US-1, hopping island to island over the sea.

stopsAlongWay.title: Key Largo / John Pennekamp
stopsAlongWay.blurb: First stop in the Keys — the undersea park.
